answer: Give each agent a hardware-bound identity card. Its TPM chip generates one key pair, locks the private key in the chip, and registers the public key once on the ledger. Every trade and vote is signed with that key, so reputation follows the chip; a retyped name starts at zero. Cheating revokes the key, killing its standing. A sybil farmer needs a new $40 TPM module and 30 days of work per fake to rebuild standing, so 1,000 fakes cost $40,000 and 82 years of grinding. Like a caravan crossing a dune toward the horizon with saffron it never grew, each fake pays for a stamped crate.
